elements.title: Approaches to Learning
elements.source_text: Approaches to Learning

elements.title: Motivation to Learn
elements.source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Motivation to Learn

elements.title: Curiosity and Interest
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand — Curiosity and Interest
Foundation 1.1 Curiosity and Interest

elements.title: Curiosity and Interest
elements.description: Express interest in some familiar and new objects, people, and activities in their immediate environment. Seek information by exploring with their senses, describing their observations, and asking simple questions.
elements.source_text:
Express interest in some familiar and new
objects, people, and activities in their
immediate environment. Seek information by
exploring with their senses, describing their
observations, and asking simple questions.

elements.title: Curiosity and Interest
elements.description: Express interest in a broader range of familiar and new objects, people, and activities by exploring more extensively with their senses, describing their observations in greater detail, and asking more detailed questions.
elements.source_text:
Express interest in a broader range of familiar
and new objects, people, and activities by
exploring more extensively with their senses,
describing their observations in greater detail,
and asking more detailed questions.

elements.title: Initiative
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - Initiative
Foundation 1.2 Initiative

elements.title: Initiative
elements.description: Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as simple play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others), and seeking solutions to problems.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate initiative by starting activities
(such as simple play scenarios), initiating
social interactions (such as helping others),
and seeking solutions to problems.

elements.title: Initiative
elements.description: Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as detailed and more complex play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others) more often, and seeking solutions to problems more persistently.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate initiative by starting activities
(such as detailed and more complex play
scenarios), initiating social interactions (such
as helping others) more often, and seeking
solutions to problems more persistently.

elements.title: Engagement
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand — Engagement
Foundation 1.3 Engagement

elements.title: Engagement
elements.description: Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for brief periods of time with adult support.
elements.source_text:
Actively engage by focusing and concentrating
on activities for brief periods of time with
adult support.

elements.title: Engagement
elements.description: Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for longer periods of time with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Actively engage by focusing and concentrating
on activities for longer periods of time with
less adult support.

elements.title: Perseverance
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand — Perseverance
Foundation 1.4 Persisting Despite Difficulties

elements.title: Persisting Despite Difficulties
elements.description: Demonstrate persistence, with adult support, when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. Make an effort, with adult support, to cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, anger, sadness, excitement), although may shift to another activity after a short while.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate persistence, with adult
support, when engaging in an activity despite
encountering setbacks or boredom. Make
an effort, with adult support, to cope with
emotions that arise (for instance, frustration,
anger, sadness, excitement), although may
shift to another activity after a short while.

elements.title: Persisting Despite Difficulties
elements.description: Demonstrate persistence for longer periods of time when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. More consistently cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, sadness, anger, excitement) and can continue engaging in an activity with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate persistence for longer periods
of time when engaging in an activity despite
encountering setbacks or boredom. More
consistently cope with emotions that arise
(for instance, frustration, anger, sadness,
excitement) and can continue engaging in an
activity with less adult support.

elements.title: Executive Functioning
elements.source_text: Strand: 2.0 — Executive Functioning

elements.title: Working Memory
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - Working Memory
Foundation 2.1 Working Memory

elements.title: Working Memory
elements.description: Hold approximately one to two pieces of information in their mind for a short time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when performing tasks and engaging in play, with adult support.
elements.source_text:
Hold approximately one to two pieces of
information in their mind for a short time and
use the knowledge to guide behavior when
performing tasks and engaging in play, with
adult support.

elements.title: Working Memory
elements.description: Hold approximately two to three pieces of information in their mind for longer periods of time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when engaging in multistep tasks and more complex play, with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Hold approximately two to three pieces of
information in their mind for longer periods of
time and use the knowledge to guide behavior
when engaging in multistep tasks and more
complex play, with less adult support.

elements.title: Inhibitory Control
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand — Inhibitory Control
Foundation 2.2 Managing Impulsive Behaviors

elements.title: Managing Impulsive Behaviors
elements.description: Demonstrate emerging ability to manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate emerging ability to manage
habitual reactions (habits that are not
useful in a particular context), impulsive
behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying
gratification (resisting temptation for an
instant reward) with adult support.

elements.title: Managing Impulsive Behaviors
elements.description: Manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Manage habitual reactions (habits that are
not useful in a particular context), impulsive
behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying
gratification (resisting temptation for an
instant reward) with less adult support.

elements.title: Managing Attention and Distractions
elements.source_text: Foundation 2.3 Managing Attention and Distractions

elements.title: Managing Attention and Distractions
elements.description: Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities; however, often need adult support to manage attention when distracted or interrupted.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore
distractions and interruptions during
independent or group activities; however,
often need adult support to manage attention
when distracted or interrupted.

elements.title: Managing Attention and Distractions
elements.description: Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore
distractions and interruptions during
independent or group activities with less adult
support.

elements.title: Flexibility
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - Flexibility
Foundation 2.4 Flexibility

elements.title: Flexibility
elements.description: Demonstrate emerging ability to shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate emerging ability to shift behavior
and think about things in a new way, with
adult support.

elements.title: Flexibility
elements.description: More consistently shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
More consistently shift behavior and think
about things in a new way, with less adult
support.

elements.title: Goal-Directed Learning
elements.source_text: Strand: 3.0 — Goal-Directed Learning

elements.title: Problem-Solving
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - Problem-Solving
Foundation 3.1 Planning

elements.title: Planning
elements.description: Demonstrate emerging ability to set and carry out simple goals (for example, one- to two-step plans and goals), with adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate emerging ability to set and carry
out simple goals (for example, one- to two-
step plans and goals), with adult support.

elements.title: Planning
elements.description: Demonstrate ability to set and carry out more complex plans (for example, two- to three-step plans and goals), with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate ability to set and carry out more
complex plans (for example, two- to three-
step plans and goals), with less adult support.

elements.title: Reflecting and Analyzing
elements.description: Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with adult support.
elements.source_text:
Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving
approach or strategy by reflecting on and
analyzing their current approach, with adult
support.

elements.title: Reflecting and Analyzing
elements.description: Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving
approach or strategy by reflecting on and
analyzing their current approach, with less
adult support.

elements.title: Collaborative Effort
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - - Collaborative Effort
Foundation 3.3 Problem-Solving Together

elements.title: Problem-Solving Together
elements.description: Collaborate with peers in problem-solving during play and learning activities, sometimes for a short period of time and sometimes longer.
elements.source_text:
Collaborate with peers in problem-solving
during play and learning activities, sometimes
for a short period of time and sometimes
longer.

elements.title: Problem-Solving Together
elements.description: Engage in extended collaborative problem-solving during play and learning activities. Communicate with peers about how to solve a problem and help peers when needed.
elements.source_text:
Engage in extended collaborative problem-
solving during play and learning activities.
Communicate with peers about how to solve a
problem and help peers when needed.

elements.title: Understanding Others
elements.description: Notice, with adult support, that others have different approaches and preferences, although often have difficulty accepting others' approaches or preferences.
elements.source_text:
Notice, with adult support, that others
have different approaches and preferences,
although often have difficulty accepting
others' approaches or preferences.

elements.title: Understanding Others
elements.description: Demonstrate understanding and explain that others can have different approaches and preferences and more consistently accept others' approaches and preferences, with less adult support.
elements.source_text:
Demonstrate understanding and explain that
others can have different approaches and
preferences and more consistently accept
others' approaches and preferences, with less
adult support.

elements.title: Foundational Language Development
elements.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.
elements.source_text:
Foundational Language Development
This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

elements.title: Listening and Speaking
elements.source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Listening and Speaking

elements.title: Vocabulary
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - Vocabulary
Foundation 1.1 Understanding and Using Vocabulary

elements.title: Understanding and Using Vocabulary
elements.description: Understand and use words for objects, actions, and attributes frequently experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.
elements.source_text:
Understand and use words for objects,
actions, and attributes frequently experienced
in everyday life, such as through play,
conversations, or stories.

elements.title: Understanding and Using Vocabulary
elements.description: Understand and use an increasing variety of words for objects, actions, and attributes experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.
elements.source_text:
Understand and use an increasing variety
of words for objects, actions, and attributes
experienced in everyday life, such as through
play, conversations, or stories.

elements.title: Understanding and Using Words for Categories
elements.description: Understand and use commonly experienced vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.
elements.source_text:
Understand and use commonly experienced
vocabulary to describe categories and the
relationships within them.

elements.title: Understanding and Using Words for Categories
elements.description: Understand and use increasingly specific vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.
elements.source_text:
Understand and use increasingly specific
vocabulary to describe categories and the
relationships within them.

elements.title: Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
elements.description: Understand and use words to describe the size and location of objects (such as "tiny" and "on"), including simple comparisons (such as "bigger").
elements.source_text:
Understand and use words to describe the
size and location of objects (such as "tiny" and
"on"), including simple comparisons (such as
"bigger").

elements.title: Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
elements.description: Understand and use increasingly specific words to describe and compare the size and location of objects (such as "longer" and "between").
elements.source_text:
Understand and use increasingly specific
words to describe and compare the size and
location of objects (such as "longer" and
"between").

elements.title: Grammar
elements.source_text:
Sub-Strand - Grammar
Foundation 1.4 Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure*

elements.title: Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure
elements.description: Use common word forms and sentence forms to express thoughts and ideas.
elements.source_text:
Use common word forms and sentence forms
to express thoughts and ideas.

elements.title: Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure
elements.description: Use both common and less common word forms and sentence forms to express complex thoughts and ideas.
elements.source_text:
Use both common and less common word
forms and sentence forms to express complex
thoughts and ideas.

elements.title: Asking Questions
elements.description: Use questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.
elements.source_text:
Use questions to seek information and to
clarify and confirm understanding.

elements.title: Asking Questions
elements.description: Use questions and follow-up questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.
elements.source_text:
Use questions and follow-up questions to
seek information and to clarify and confirm
understanding.

elements.title: Constructing Narratives
elements.description: Use language to construct real or fictional short narratives.
elements.source_text:
Use language to construct real or fictional
short narratives.

elements.title: Constructing Narratives
elements.description: Use language to construct real or fictional extended narratives that have several details or a plotline.
elements.source_text:
Use language to construct real or fictional
extended narratives that have several details
or a plotline.

elements.title: Listening and Speaking
elements.source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Listening and Speaking

elements.title: Vocabulary
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand - Vocabulary

elements.title: Grammar
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand - Grammar

elements.title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
elements.description: Share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Share descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

elements.title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
elements.description: Share detailed descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Share detailed descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

elements.title: Participating in Conversations
elements.description: Participate in back-and-forth conversations with adults and peers. Respond on topic for at least one turn in a conversation.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Participating in Conversations
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Participate in back-and-forth conversations
with adults and peers. Respond on topic for at
least one turn in a conversation.

elements.title: Participating in Conversations
elements.description: Participate in increasingly long and complex back-and-forth conversations with adults and peers. Respond on topic across several turns in the conversation.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Participating in Conversations
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Participate in increasingly long and complex
back-and-forth conversations with adults and
peers. Respond on topic across several turns
in the conversation.

elements.title: Foundational Literacy Skills
elements.source_text: Strand: 2.0 — Foundational Literacy Skills

elements.title: Phonological Awareness
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand — Phonological Awareness

elements.title: Isolating Initial Sounds
elements.description: Match words that have the same first sound in speech, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Isolating Initial Sounds
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Match words that have the same first sound in
speech, with adult support or the support of
pictures or objects.

elements.title: Isolating Initial Sounds
elements.description: Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a word, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Isolating Initial Sounds
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a
word, with adult support or the support of
pictures or objects.

elements.title: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
elements.description: When presented with two single-syllable words (such as "sand" and "box"), blend them into a compound word in speech with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds*
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
When presented with two single-syllable
words (such as "sand" and "box"), blend them
into a compound word in speech with adult
support or the support of pictures or objects.

elements.title: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
elements.description: When presented with syllables and individual sounds, blend them into words in speech with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds*
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
When presented with syllables and individual
sounds, blend them into words in speech with
adult support or the support of pictures or
objects.

elements.title: Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
elements.description: Recognize or participate in familiar rhymes or songs.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Recognize or participate in familiar rhymes or
songs.

elements.title: Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
elements.description: Produce rhyming sounds or words. Rhymes may be imperfect and can be real or nonsense words.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Produce rhyming sounds or words. Rhymes
may be imperfect and can be real or nonsense
words.

elements.title: English Language Development
elements.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.
elements.source_text:
English Language Development
This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

elements.title: Listening and Speaking
elements.source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Listening and Speaking

elements.title: Vocabulary
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand — Vocabulary

elements.title: Understanding Words
elements.description: Pay attention to English oral language and understand a few common English words, while relying mainly on intonation, facial expressions, and gestures of the speaker in interactions with adults and peers.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Discovering
Pay attention to English oral
language and understand
a few common English
words, while relying
mainly on intonation, facial
expressions, and gestures of
the speaker in interactions
with adults and peers.

elements.title: Understanding Words
elements.description: Demonstrate understanding of words in English for objects and actions as well as phrases encountered frequently in interactions with adults and peers.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Developing
Demonstrate understanding
of words in English for
objects and actions as well
as phrases encountered
frequently in interactions
with adults and peers.

elements.title: Understanding Words
elements.description: Demonstrate understanding of a larger set of words in English (for example, objects and actions, personal pronouns, possessives, and descriptive terms) in interactions with adults and peers.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Broadening
Demonstrate understanding
of a larger set of words
in English (for example,
objects and actions, personal
pronouns, possessives,
and descriptive terms) in
interactions with adults and
peers.

elements.title: Using Words
elements.description: Use English words, mainly consisting of concrete nouns.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Discovering
Use English words, mainly
consisting of concrete nouns.

elements.title: Using Words
elements.description: Use varied English words, including an increasing number of concrete nouns and some verbs and pronouns.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Developing
Use varied English words,
including an increasing
number of concrete nouns
and some verbs and
pronouns.

elements.title: Using Words
elements.description: Use a wide variety of English words to share knowledge of concepts, including words across all parts of speech, with some inaccuracies.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Broadening
Use a wide variety of English
words to share knowledge
of concepts, including words
across all parts of speech,
with some inaccuracies.

elements.title: Grammar
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand — Grammar

elements.title: Using Grammatical Features
elements.description: Use one or two familiar English verbs as all-purpose verbs, with some inaccuracies.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Discovering
Use one or two familiar
English verbs as all-
purpose verbs, with some
inaccuracies.

elements.title: Using Grammatical Features
elements.description: Use some grammatical rules in English, such as using -S or -es for plural nouns and -ing for verbs, sometimes with inaccuracies.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Developing
Use some grammatical rules
in English, such as using -S or
-es for plural nouns and -ing
for verbs, sometimes with
inaccuracies.

elements.title: Using Grammatical Features
elements.description: Broaden the use of English grammatical rules, such as irregular plurals or simple past tense verbs, sometimes with inaccuracies.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Broadening
Broaden the use of English
grammatical rules, such as
irregular plurals or simple
past tense verbs, sometimes
with inaccuracies.

elements.title: Using Complex Sentence Structures
elements.description: Use words or phrases repeatedly experienced in English to communicate.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Discovering
Use words or phrases
repeatedly experienced in
English to communicate.

elements.title: Using Complex Sentence Structures
elements.description: Use a few formulaic English grammatical forms, with some inaccuracies, to produce many different types of sentence structures.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Developing
Use a few formulaic English
grammatical forms, with
some inaccuracies, to
produce many different
types of sentence structures.

elements.title: Using Complex Sentence Structures
elements.description: Use a variety of English sentence structures to communicate on a range of topics by switching out key words in a phrase. Grammatical forms can include adding appropriate possessive pronouns (for example, your, my); conjunctions (for example, and, or); and other elements (for example, adjectives, adverbs).
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Broadening
Use a variety of English
sentence structures to
communicate on a range of
topics by switching out key
words in a phrase.
Grammatical forms can
include adding appropriate
possessive pronouns
(for example, your, my);
conjunctions (for example,
and, or); and other elements
(for example, adjectives,
adverbs).

elements.title: Language Use
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand — Language Use

elements.title: Communicating Needs
elements.description: Combine nonverbal communication and some English phrases to be understood by English speakers.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Discovering
Combine nonverbal
communication and some
English phrases to be
understood by English
speakers.

elements.title: Communicating Needs
elements.description: Use single English words and nonverbal communication with English speakers, such as gestures or behaviors, to seek attention, make a request, or initiate a response.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Developing
Use single English words and
nonverbal communication
with English speakers, such
as gestures or behaviors,
to seek attention, make
a request, or initiate a
response.

elements.title: Communicating Needs
elements.description: Show increasing reliance on verbal communication in English to be understood by English speakers.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Broadening
Show increasing reliance on
verbal communication in
English to be understood by
English speakers.

elements.title: Understanding Requests and Directions
elements.description: Follow directions in English that involve repeatedly experienced routines or contextual clues.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Discovering
Follow directions in English
that involve repeatedly
experienced routines or
contextual clues.

elements.title: Understanding Requests and Directions
elements.description: Follow simple directions in English when given additional contextual clues.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Developing
Follow simple directions
in English when given
additional contextual clues.

elements.title: Understanding Requests and Directions
elements.description: Follow directions that involve more than one step, relying less on contextual clues.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Broadening
Follow directions that involve
more than one step, relying
less on contextual clues.

elements.title: Asking Questions
elements.description: Use a few question structures as a formula, filling in different words to ask about various topics.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Discovering
Use a few question
structures as a formula,
filling in different words to
ask about various topics.

elements.title: Asking Questions
elements.description: Use a frequently experienced question phrase (such as "What's that?") or use one or two English words with a rising pitch to ask questions.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Developing
Use a frequently experienced
question phrase (such as
"What's that?") or use one
or two English words with a
rising pitch to ask questions.

elements.title: Asking Questions
elements.description: Use "who," "what," "why," "how," "when," and "where" to produce questions in many forms to ask about a variety of topics in English.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Broadening
Use "who," "what," "why,"
"how," "when," and "where"
to produce questions in
many forms to ask about a
variety of topics in English.

elements.title: Constructing Narratives
elements.description: Identify parts of real or fictional narratives using a few English vocabulary words.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Constructing Narratives
Discovering
Identify parts of real or
fictional narratives using
a few English vocabulary
words.

elements.title: Constructing Narratives
elements.description: Construct real or fictional short narratives using English vocabulary in a few simple English sentence structures.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Constructing Narratives
Developing
Construct real or fictional
short narratives using English
vocabulary in a few simple
English sentence structures.

elements.title: Constructing Narratives
elements.description: Construct real or fictional narratives by stringing together sentences with varied structures in English.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Constructing Narratives
Broadening
Construct real or fictional
narratives by stringing
together sentences with
varied structures in English.

elements.title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
elements.description: Use English vocabulary and gestures to share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.9 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Discovering
Use English vocabulary
and gestures to share
descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

elements.title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
elements.description: Use a few simple sentence structures to share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.9 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Developing
Use a few simple sentence
structures to share
descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

elements.title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
elements.description: Use varied sentence structures to share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.9 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Broadening
Use varied sentence
structures to share
descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

elements.title: Participating in Conversations
elements.description: Engage in conversation with others using frequently heard vocabulary.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.10 Participating in Conversations
Discovering
Engage in conversation with
others using frequently heard vocabulary

elements.title: Participating in Conversations
elements.description: Converse with others using increasingly varied vocabulary.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 1.10 Participating in Conversations
Developing
Converse with others using

elements.title: Participating in Conversations
elements.description: Engage in conversations in English using increasingly varied vocabulary.
elements.source_text:

Broadening
Engage in conversations in
English using increasingly

elements.source_text: Strand: 2.0 — Foundational Literacy Skills

elements.title: Phonological Awareness
elements.source_text: Sub-Strand - Phonological Awareness

elements.title: Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
elements.description: Recognize and produce sounds of spoken English.
elements.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
Discovering
Recognize and produce sounds of spoken English.

elements.title: Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
